"I could scarce credit your narrative at first," continued Dr. Merton, adjusting his spectacles with a hand that trembled slightly, "but having examined the locality myself, I am constrained to admit that the evidence of... unnatural presence is considerable. The scorched earth, the peculiar odor still lingering, and those marks upon the trees—"

"Which ain't natural marks, neither," Hank interjected, his voice dropping to something barely above a whisper. "Nor the sounds as comes after dark, doctor. Nor the way the dogs won't go near the place."

       *       *       *       *       *

It was early in the afternoon, for they had traveled quickly, and there
were still a good two hours of daylight left. Dr. Cathcart and Hank lost
no time in beginning the search, but Simpson was too exhausted to
accompany them. They would follow the blazed marks on the trees, and
where possible, his footsteps. Meanwhile the best thing he could do was
to keep a good fire going, and rest.

But after something like three hours' search, the darkness already down,
the two men returned to camp with nothing to report.
